sampling_model.design: A novel calibration-plus-marginals design: an aligned calibration sample supplies \(n_S\) joint observations for views in \(S\), and each view supplies a viewwise sample containing its calibration observations when available together with any additional observations from the same target population.
sampling_model.units: Observations are independent and identically distributed across units within each source. The calibration sample and every viewwise source have the corresponding marginal law of the same target \(P\); they need not be mutually independent because calibration units may also enter marginal estimators. Cross-source independence holds only for disjoint cohorts.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no treatment variable; the causal target is the shared-order structural coefficient family and its invariant ancestry.
sampling_model.overlap: Alignment is required only among views in \(S\); no cross-view block involving an unselected view is observed. Signal-dependent selection, population transport, and source-specific target laws are excluded.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Empirical covariance blocks are estimated from the aligned and viewwise samples without assuming independence across block estimators; modified-Cholesky regressions and Schur states are recomputed for each moment collection in the confidence region.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Section 4.6, Assumption 2 requires edgewise within-view correlation and unequal absolute cross-view correlations between each cause and the corresponding effect disturbance; Theorem 3 identifies the causal partial order and every view-specific coefficient matrix, with its Assumption 3 additionally identifying a total order.

Section 3.1, Lemma 1 characterizes an exogenous variable by independence from all pairwise-regression residuals, Lemma 2 shows that residualizing one true exogenous variable yields another LiNGAM, and Corollary 1 preserves the remaining causal order.

Section 2 assumes multiple non-Gaussian LiNGAM datasets with a shared causal order and possibly different coefficient matrices, and Section 3.2 jointly selects successive variables by aggregating residual-independence scores across the unpaired groups.

Equation (2), Theorem 4.1, and Theorem 4.3 identify individual linear acyclic models through shared environment components using Shared ICA, under at most one Gaussian component or a cross-individual noise-variance diversity condition.
The multi-domain linear-SEM procedure exploits shared causal structure and domain-wise heterogeneity to recover a common graph from separate domain datasets.
Its pair condition is sufficient for full linear-model identification and worst-case necessary when intervention experiments observe overlapping variable sets.
Its recursive algorithm partitions an MPDAG class into subclasses with pairwise distinct total-effect functionals.
Its maximum-cardinality-search procedure enumerates every graph-distinct DAG in a Markov equivalence class with linear delay.
Equivalence classes defined by local colors in a decomposable acyclic AND--OR graph can be enumerated with polynomial delay.
A locally searchable parent relation can enumerate a connected family without retaining a global visited set.
A minimum intervention-target family guaranteeing full DAG identifiability can be constructed through separating systems on chordal chain components.
Minimum-cost intervention design is NP-hard and admits approximation guarantees through graph separating systems.
A recursively reduced identifiable linear SEM admits Schur-complement updates and finite-sample recovery under an explicit score gap.
Gaussian singular-value concentration yields nonasymptotic operator-norm control of sample covariance matrices.
Criterion inversion yields consistent estimators and confidence regions for identified parameter sets under separation conditions.
Missingness graphs characterize recoverability and testability of probabilistic queries under systematic missingness.
The Cam-CAN repository documents modality-specific MRI and MEG acquisition across a lifespan cohort.

body.tldr: For any preassigned pair of views, two-view calibration generically identifies the common order and every view-specific coefficient matrix on the explicitly restrictive component-aligned Gaussian subclass. The failure locus is an explicit proper algebraic set: each wrong order supplies a denominator-cleared residual polynomial, and a single-edge unequal-correlation witness proves that polynomial is nonzero. Thus two views attain the full-calibration singleton outside a Lebesgue-null set without edge minimality or the diversity assumption used by Heurtebise et al. A fixed-order residual lemma, path-independent removed-set recursion, computational hitting-set corollary, and covariance-region inversion support the headline. Equality examples lie on the exceptional set, including a law with one full-calibration tuple but two tuples for the pair \(\{1,2\}\). Duplicate-free output-sensitive traversal remains the open-ended question.

project_justification.gap: Heurtebise et al.'s Section 4.6, Assumption 2 and Theorem 3 give full-pair identification under edgewise correlation diversity on their broader disturbance class. DirectLiNGAM Section 3.1, Lemmas 1--2 and Corollary 1 justify recursive removal of one true exogenous variable. Shimizu's JointLiNGAM, Chen et al.'s individual-structure method, and Ghassami et al.'s multi-domain procedure borrow information across datasets or domains through non-Gaussianity, shared-population components, or shared structure with domain heterogeneity. None proves that an arbitrary pair fixed in advance attains full-calibration identification generically on a component-aligned Gaussian parameter space, locates every failure on a proper algebraic variety, or characterizes all surviving orders on that variety.
project_justification.niche: On the component-aligned subclass, finite-dimensional Gaussianity makes every fixed-order coefficient family observable from marginal modified Cholesky factors, while selected paired cross-blocks provide exact order-dependent orthogonality equations. This separates marginal coefficient recovery from the scarce paired information needed only for order discrimination.
project_justification.fill: The headline theorem clears the positive principal-minor denominators of every wrong-order residual restriction, proves nonvanishing by an explicit single-edge witness, and concludes that any preassigned view pair gives the full-view singleton outside a Lebesgue-null algebraic set. Supporting results supply fixed-order completion, complete path-independent recursion, equality-locus examples, a computational calibration certificate, and covariance-region inversion with explicit local stability moduli.

body.related_work: HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM is the flagship model anchor. Its Section 4.6, Assumption 2 requires, for every union-graph edge, a view pair with nonzero within-view cause--effect correlation and unequal absolute cross-view correlations for the cause and effect disturbance; its Theorem 3 identifies the causal partial order and all view-specific coefficient matrices from full pairing, with Assumption 3 adding a unique total order. On the intersection of its standing assumptions and Assumption 2 with the narrower component-aligned subclass, its full-pair singleton agrees with \(\Theta_M(\mathcal O_M)\) and the induced partial order; this is a restricted-domain consistency comparison only. The headline addresses a different observation regime: on the narrower class, any pair fixed before observing parameters equals the full-calibration singleton off an explicit proper algebraic set, without imposing edge minimality or Heurtebise et al.'s diversity assumption. The fixed-order residual iff is supporting infrastructure, not the principal novelty. ShimizuEtAl2011DirectLiNGAM is the recursive-residual comparator: Section 3.1, Lemma 1 finds one exogenous variable by residual independence, Lemma 2 preserves LiNGAM after removing that true root, and Corollary 1 preserves the remaining order. It does not prove removed-set path independence across different valid paths or characterize all compatible roots and complete compatible orders. The recursive proof behind Heurtebise et al.'s Theorem 3 likewise follows roots licensed by its diversity score and lacks those complete-frontier steps. Shimizu2012JointLiNGAM pools residual-independence information across unpaired non-Gaussian groups with a shared order. ChenEtAl2024IndividualCausal identifies individual structures through shared population components and Shared ICA under non-Gaussianity or noise-variance diversity. GhassamiEtAl2018MultiDomain uses domain-wise heterogeneity and shared causal structure across separate datasets. Those mechanisms differ from selected paired covariance blocks and do not return an exact possibly non-singleton compatibility set on algebraic equality loci. HyttinenEberhardtHoyer2012Overlapping studies pair conditions for experimental total effects, not paired-view residual covariances. GuoPerkovic2021MinimalEffects, WienobstEtAl2023MECEnumeration, WangEtAl2023EquivalenceEnumeration, and AvisFukuda1996ReverseSearch inform the open quotient-enumeration question without establishing a local congruence for numerical coefficient tuples. HauserBuhlmann2014ActiveLearning and LindgrenEtAl2018CostAware motivate only the separator analogy behind the computational hitting-set corollary. GhoshalHonorio2018LinearSEM uses precision-based recursive gaps rather than the residual and path-product margins here. Vershynin2018HighDimensionalProbability supplies Gaussian covariance concentration, and ChernozhukovHongTamer2007SetInference supplies general set inversion. MohanPearl2021MissingData motivates the exclusion of selection and transport. TaylorEtAl2017CamCAN documents a future diagnostic use case but does not validate component alignment or common-target calibration sampling.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The generic theorem is relative to the fixed-order finite-dimensional parameterization and gives no uniform distance from \(\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}\); near that variety, finite-sample order recovery can be unstable. Equality examples are genuine points on the exceptional set. In particular, \(P_{\mathrm{ex}}\in\mathcal E_{12,(1,2)}\) has two tuples for \(S=\{1,2\}\) although full pairing leaves one. The \(2^p\)-state result counts exact-real arithmetic operations and does not by itself give polynomial bit complexity. Exact rational \(p=m=3\) enumeration agreed with dynamic-programming leaves for every admissible calibration subset. The desired exact-once output bound remains confined to \(\text{oeq:output-sensitive-quotient}\). At population moments, \(d_*>0\) falsifies the maintained class on observed calibration blocks. In samples, rejection is warranted only when a simultaneous lower confidence bound for \(d_*\) is positive; non-rejection is not validation and says nothing about unobserved pairs.
body.honest_scope: Generic two-view sufficiency, the proper algebraic exceptional set, fixed-order completion, the strictness witness, removed-set recursion, essential poset, local stability modulus, and covariance inversion are proof obligations on the component-aligned Gaussian subclass. The residual compatibility iff and calibration hitting-set iff are supporting consequences, not headline novelty. Genericity is relative to coefficients respecting a fixed \(\pi_0\) and positive-definite coordinate disturbance covariances; it neither supplies a uniform margin nor identifies points on \(\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}\). Joint Gaussianity and component alignment exclude broader LiMVAMs, and positive-definite \(\Gamma_i\) excludes singular shared-noise limits. The repeated-sensor mechanism applies only to coordinate-aligned measurements. Calibration-plus-marginals sampling is sourcewise independent and identically distributed from one target population but need not make covariance estimators independent; selection and transport remain outside the model. The comparison with Heurtebise et al. is restricted to the intersection with their standing assumptions and Assumption 2. For \(\tau>0\), \(\Pi_S^{(\tau)}\) and \(\Theta_S^{(\tau)}\) are sensitivity envelopes, not unrestricted-class identified sets. Cam-CAN MEG and fMRI remain future diagnostic use cases. Output-sensitive quotient enumeration remains open.
